differences.impact: Dark-mode page content keeps its original colours, like the upstream viewer.
Page glyph edges soften like the reference; CSS filters do not change the image box, so the page geometry landmarks are unchanged.

differences.evidence: packages/vue-pdf/src/components/PdfViewer.vue:2129 keeps only `.pdf-body { flex-direction: column }` at container width <= 760px; `.pdf-frame-wrap` keeps its 24px padding at every width, matching upstream `PAGE_GAP = 24` (pdf-viewer.tsx:172,2924).
differences.impact: The page frame no longer shifts by 12px at 768/390; the page1 landmark delta is inside its 1px tolerance.

differences.evidence: Reference page frame is 595.266 x 841.875 CSS px, ours 595 x 841.281 (capture report `geometry.landmarks.page1`).
differences.impact: Sub-pixel rounding of the zoom-1 page size; contributes to raster diff but stays under the 1px landmark budget.

differences.evidence: packages/vue-pdf/package.json pins `@embedpdf/*@2.14.4`; the reference app uses `@embedpdf/*@2.15.0` (tools/extend-reference/package.json).
differences.impact: The page bitmap rasterisation (text hinting, tiling, page-size rounding) can differ even when both sides paint the same PDF bytes. This is why the blocking route gate covers chrome-only pixels plus geometry, and keeps full-page pixels as a diagnostic.
